explained.tdh.proofs.meta.title: Zero-knowledge proofs of a TDH day: what is proved so far
explained.tdh.proofs.meta.description: What a zero-knowledge proof of a TDH day shows, why two programs must prove it, what has been proved so far, and what has not.
explained.tdh.proofs.h1: What a proof of a day shows, what is proved so far, and what is not.
explained.tdh.proofs.lede: A zero-knowledge proof of a day would let anyone check, in one call to Ethereum, that its TDH follows from Ethereum's own blocks; the proof files are not public yet.
explained.tdh.proofs.verdict.headline: Program A's run of {date} is proved, and mainnet's SP1 verifier accepts the proof in a read-only call.
explained.tdh.proofs.verdict.body: The proof says its {words} words follow from blocks that hash forward to anchor block {anchor}, and from the history before them. Checking that anchor against Ethereum is the contract's step, and the contract is not deployed. One GPU worked {hours} h {minutes} min to prove what the same code computes in {seconds} s without a proof.
explained.tdh.proofs.verdict.bodyB: Program B, written separately, ran the same day and got the same words, all but the anchor. It has not proved them.
explained.tdh.proofs.verdict.pairV14: Under TDH v1.4, both programs proved one common test cycle on {date}, and mainnet's verifiers accept both proofs in a read-only call. No mainnet day is proved by both yet.
explained.tdh.proofs.verdict.limitBody: The contract records a day only with proofs from both programs. It is built and tested on a local copy of mainnet, and not deployed: deploying is the owner's decision ({decision}).
explained.tdh.proofs.verdict.withBurn: All three leave out the burn addresses. Counting them gives {total}: two right totals for one day.
explained.tdh.proofs.verdict.source: From the proof's public values, {bytes} bytes; accepted in a read-only call at block {block}.
explained.tdh.proofs.sim.headline: The contract refuses a pair whose outputs differ in any word but the anchor.
explained.tdh.proofs.sim.body: Here program B's total is one TDH above program A's. The contract stops at its second check and records nothing; it never reaches the proofs.
explained.tdh.proofs.sim.eqLabel: Total TDH, word {word} of each output
explained.tdh.proofs.drift: Program A's proof of {date} and the first pair are under the rules' earlier version, {old}, from before four wallets (D136) and the name TDH v1.4 (D137), so a TDH v1.4 deployment refuses them. Under {ruleId}, both programs have proved a common test cycle, not yet a mainnet day.

explained.tdh.proofs.record.first.title: First proofs
explained.tdh.proofs.record.first.body: Each program proved one small test day. Mainnet's verifiers accepted each proof, on a local copy.
explained.tdh.proofs.record.pair.title: The first pair
explained.tdh.proofs.record.pair.body: Both programs proved one common test cycle. The contract accepted the pair for {gas} gas.
explained.tdh.proofs.record.day.title: A real day, half proved
explained.tdh.proofs.record.day.body: Program A proved {date} in {hours} h {minutes} min on one GPU.
explained.tdh.proofs.record.v14.title: The pair under TDH v1.4
explained.tdh.proofs.record.v14.body: Rebuilt on the new rule ID, both programs proved test cycle {cycle}. Mainnet's verifiers accept both proofs.

explained.tdh.proofs.record.next.body: A mainnet day proved by both programs, and a deployment once the owner approves one.
explained.tdh.proofs.s1.label: What a proof is
explained.tdh.proofs.s1.heading: The program checks Ethereum; the proof shows the program ran.
explained.tdh.proofs.s1.p1: Program A reads a day of Ethereum, {bytes} bytes of it. It checks every block of the day against the chain of block hashes, replays TDH over the whole history and writes {words} words, {total} bytes in all.
explained.tdh.proofs.s1.p2: SP1, a zero-knowledge virtual machine, then makes a proof of {proofBytes} bytes that this exact program wrote those exact bytes. A contract can check it in one call, for about {gas} gas, without running anything again. Zero-knowledge hides nothing here; what matters is that the proof is small and cheap to check.
explained.tdh.proofs.words.label: The {words} words
explained.tdh.proofs.words.question: What exactly does proof A state about {date}?
explained.tdh.proofs.words.say.day: What the statement is about: its kind, this network, the cycle and the rule's ID. The contract takes only its own network and its one rule, and only the cycle after the last one it recorded.
explained.tdh.proofs.words.say.start: Where the day starts: the last block and the whole history of the day before. The contract records a day only if these equal the day it recorded last, so no day can be skipped or swapped.
explained.tdh.proofs.words.say.end: Where the day ends: the last block stamped before midnight UTC, and the hash of the block after it, which shows the cut is in the right place.
explained.tdh.proofs.words.say.anchor: A later block whose hash Ethereum itself reports. Every header from the day's start is hashed forward to it, which makes the blocks Ethereum's and not made up. Each program picks its own anchor.
explained.tdh.proofs.words.say.read: What the day was computed from: a root over every log of the four contracts that count, from their deployment to the day's end, and a hash of the claim limits it read from Ethereum's state for cards still under the edition floor.
explained.tdh.proofs.words.say.result: The day's TDH: a root over every wallet's record, the counts, the total, and the cycle root that validators sign. The contract recomputes the cycle root from the other words.
explained.tdh.proofs.words.brokenSay: Program B, written separately, ran the same day in its zkVM. Every word matches program A's but the two anchor words: each program picks its own anchor, and the contract checks each one on its own. Any other difference is refused.
explained.tdh.proofs.words.ruleSource: P53 §4.6: one ABI word of {wordBytes} bytes each, {bytes} bytes in all.
explained.tdh.proofs.words.aria: The words of proof A's statement for {date}, group by group
explained.tdh.proofs.s2.label: How a proof is made
explained.tdh.proofs.s2.heading: Half the work proves that nothing was left out.
explained.tdh.proofs.s2.p1: A day of Ethereum has thousands of blocks. For each one, the program needs evidence that it missed no log of the four contracts that count. Either the block's bloom filter rules them out, or every receipt of the block is rebuilt into the root its header commits to.
explained.tdh.proofs.s2.p2: In the cycle dated {date}, the day that ended at its midnight, only {txBlocks} of {blocks} blocks held one of the day's {logs} logs that count. Showing that the rest held none is about half the work.

explained.tdh.proofs.lanes.eth.title: The day's blocks
explained.tdh.proofs.lanes.eth.cap: {blocks} blocks, and every log of the four contracts since they were deployed
explained.tdh.proofs.lanes.input.title: Headers, receipts, the history
explained.tdh.proofs.lanes.input.cap: {bytes} bytes from public Ethereum servers; every answer is checked
explained.tdh.proofs.lanes.run.title: Check, replay, write
explained.tdh.proofs.lanes.proof.title: A proof for Ethereum
explained.tdh.proofs.lanes.proof.cap: {bytes} bytes, after {hours} h {minutes} min on one {gpu} GPU
explained.tdh.proofs.lanes.verify.title: Accepts it
explained.tdh.proofs.blocks.label: The {blocks} blocks of the cycle dated {date}, by their evidence
explained.tdh.proofs.blocks.cap: Each block has exactly one form of evidence, so both programs read one input. A bloom of all zeros never counts as evidence.
explained.tdh.proofs.phases.label: Where program A's steps go
explained.tdh.proofs.phases.tdh: Replaying TDH over the whole history
explained.tdh.proofs.phases.accounting: The accounting root, a second replay
explained.tdh.proofs.phases.cap: The same day on the build before, {build}, profiled at {total} steps. The proved build took {steps}.
explained.tdh.proofs.s3.label: Why two
explained.tdh.proofs.s3.heading: Two programs, written apart, in two proof systems, must state the same day.
explained.tdh.proofs.s3.p1: A proof shows that a program ran, not that the program is right. So there are two. Program A is the validator's own code, run in SP1. Program B was written separately, from the specifications alone, and runs in RISC Zero, on different proving libraries.
explained.tdh.proofs.s3.p2: The contract would record a day only when both proofs verify and the two outputs are equal in every word but the anchor. Then a bug in one program, or a flaw in one proof system, could not get a wrong day recorded on its own.
explained.tdh.proofs.table.caption: Programs A and B, side by side
explained.tdh.proofs.table.codeA: The validator's own: its Ethereum checks, the TDH core and the commitment trees
explained.tdh.proofs.table.codeB: Written apart, from the specifications only; it never reads program A
explained.tdh.proofs.table.identityA: Key {key} under TDH v1.4; rebuilt at another path on the same machine, same key
explained.tdh.proofs.table.identityB: Image ID {image} under TDH v1.4; rebuilt at another path on the same machine, same ID
explained.tdh.proofs.table.dayA: in {hours} h {minutes} min on one GPU
explained.tdh.proofs.table.dayB: not proved; it ran in its zkVM. A mainnet day under TDH v1.4 would take a projected {low} to {high} GPU-hours
explained.tdh.proofs.table.pair: The test cycle {cycle}, under TDH v1.4
explained.tdh.proofs.case.flaw.title: A flaw in one proof system is not hypothetical.
explained.tdh.proofs.case.flaw.body: On {date}, SP1's maintainers published a soundness flaw in an earlier SP1 circuit ({id}), fixed in version {fixed}; its old routes on mainnet are frozen. A forged proof of one kind would still need a valid proof of the other.
explained.tdh.proofs.case.review.title: Writing program B already found a flaw.
explained.tdh.proofs.case.review.body: On {date}, writing program B from the specification showed that {count} of P26's test vectors reused log positions no real chain can produce. They were corrected, and every expected value stayed the same.
explained.tdh.proofs.s3.limitBody: One specification, one statement, and the wrapper both proofs use for Ethereum, {wrapper}: a break of its curve would reach both. P52 recommends another wrapper for program B; that is open.
explained.tdh.proofs.s4.label: The contract
explained.tdh.proofs.s4.heading: Built, not deployed: a day would be recorded only if every check passes, in this order.
explained.tdh.proofs.s4.p1: The contract of {decision} would take both programs' outputs and proofs in one transaction, from anyone. Once a day is recorded, any contract or wallet could read its root without trusting validators.
explained.tdh.proofs.s4.p2: One submission costs about {gas} gas: the two verifications, the comparison and the day's record.
explained.tdh.proofs.check.decoding.body: Exactly {bytes} bytes: {words} words, each within its width.
explained.tdh.proofs.check.outputs.title: Two outputs, one statement
explained.tdh.proofs.check.outputs.body: Program B's output equals program A's in every word but the anchor.
explained.tdh.proofs.check.network.title: Network, rule and horizon
explained.tdh.proofs.check.network.body: This network, the one rule it accepts, and a cycle before the programs' fork horizon, {horizon}.
explained.tdh.proofs.check.chaining.body: The cycle after the last one recorded, starting where it ended.
explained.tdh.proofs.check.time.title: Time
explained.tdh.proofs.check.time.body: The day has ended, and its last block falls inside it.
explained.tdh.proofs.check.cycleRoot.bod: Recomputed from the statement's own words.
explained.tdh.proofs.check.anchors.title: Anchors
explained.tdh.proofs.check.anchors.body: Each a block hash Ethereum itself reports.
explained.tdh.proofs.check.proofs.title: Proofs
explained.tdh.proofs.check.proofs.body: SP1's verifier for A and RISC Zero's for B, each over its own output.
explained.tdh.proofs.s4.tested: {unit} unit and fuzz tests and {fork} tests on a local copy of mainnet pass ({date}).
explained.tdh.proofs.s4.limitBody: The decision allows a deployment only when the owner approves one, and the code has no deployment script, on purpose.
explained.tdh.proofs.s5.label: Where it stands
explained.tdh.proofs.s5.heading: A real day is half proved, a test day fully proved, and nothing is recorded yet.
explained.tdh.proofs.is.day: Program A proved the day of {date}, cycle {cycle}, in {hours} h {minutes} min on one GPU. Mainnet's SP1 verifier accepts the proof in a read-only call at block {block}.
explained.tdh.proofs.is.pair: Under TDH v1.4, both programs proved one common test cycle, {cycle}, on synthetic blocks ({date}), equal in all {words} words. Mainnet's verifiers accept both proofs in a read-only call at block {block}; on a local copy of mainnet the contract accepted the pair for {gas} gas.
explained.tdh.proofs.is.b: Program B ran the day of {date} in its zkVM, and every word equals program A's but the anchor.
explained.tdh.proofs.is.tests: The contract passes {unit} unit and fuzz tests, and {fork} tests on a local copy of mainnet ({date}).
explained.tdh.proofs.isNot.deploy: Deployed. That is the owner's decision ({decision}).
explained.tdh.proofs.isNot.b: A mainnet day proved by both programs. Program A's proof of {date} is under the retired rule. Program B's day under TDH v1.4 would take a projected {low} to {high} GPU-hours, about ${cost} of rented GPUs; program A's took {hours} h {minutes} min and about ${costA}.
explained.tdh.proofs.isNot.history: Proved history. Every day rests on the history before the first proven one. Proving it from the start means about {million} million blocks and recursion, which is not built; until then a deployment's start is trusted.
explained.tdh.proofs.isNot.certificate: Proofs beside the validators' daily certificate. The validator software is at {version}, built and being tested; nothing signs yet.
explained.tdh.proofs.s6.label: What a proof guarantees
explained.tdh.proofs.s6.heading: Each layer stops one kind of mistake. None stops a mistake in the rules.
explained.tdh.proofs.s6.p1: Pick what goes wrong. The model follows it through the layers a day would pass on its way to the record, and shows where it stops, with the test that shows it. The contract is built and tested, not deployed.
explained.tdh.proofs.guard.label: What a proof guarantees
explained.tdh.proofs.guard.question: Something goes wrong. What stops it?
explained.tdh.proofs.guard.layers: The layers a day passes, and where this mistake stops
explained.tdh.proofs.layer.proofSub: binds the program to its output
explained.tdh.proofs.layer.secondSub: the same words, from code written apart
explained.tdh.proofs.layer.contractSub: rule, chain, time, cycle root, anchors
explained.tdh.proofs.say.total: Someone changes the total after the proof is made. The proof covers all {bytes} bytes, so mainnet's verifier refuses the changed bytes. Tested on the first real proofs: one flipped bit in each of the {words} words, every one refused. Changed in one output only, the contract refuses it sooner, at its second check.
explained.tdh.proofs.say.log: A data server leaves one of the day's transfers out of the input. The block's receipts no longer rebuild into the root in its header, so program A stops, and a run that stops has no proof. Tested: a valid input broken one piece at a time.
explained.tdh.proofs.say.blocks: Anyone can stack invented headers on a real block, and both programs would prove them. But the chain must end at an anchor whose hash Ethereum itself reports, and the contract would ask Ethereum. Tested: a wrong anchor hash in either output.
explained.tdh.proofs.say.bugA: Program A computes one wrong word and proves it honestly. Program B, written apart, computes the right word, and the contract refuses two outputs that differ. Tested: program B's output changed in one word.
explained.tdh.proofs.say.flaw: A flaw lets someone forge an SP1 proof. The contract would still need a valid RISC Zero proof of the same words, from a second, separate system. A flaw of this kind has been published once: SP1's {id}, after which its old routes on mainnet were frozen.
explained.tdh.proofs.say.skip: Someone submits a day that does not start where the last recorded day ended. Each day must chain to the last, block and history, so a gap or a rival history is refused. Tested: gaps, replays and competing days.
explained.tdh.proofs.say.rule: A day is proved under a rule the contract does not run. It accepts exactly one rule ID, so the first real pair, proved under the retired rule, is refused by a TDH v1.4 deployment. Tested.
explained.tdh.proofs.say.broken: The rules themselves are wrong, and both programs follow them. Both compute the same wrong number, both proofs verify and the contract records it. A proof shows that a day followed the programs; whether the rules are right is for the vectors, the Lean proofs and the daily comparison.
explained.tdh.proofs.guard.ruleSource: The contract's checks in the order it runs them; the first line is the programs' own rule, which runs before any proof exists.
explained.tdh.proofs.s7.label: What you still trust
explained.tdh.proofs.s7.heading: Trust moves from whoever computed the day to the things below.
explained.tdh.proofs.trust.systems: SP1 and RISC Zero are sound
explained.tdh.proofs.trust.systemsCovers: Two systems on different libraries, so one flaw is not enough. SP1 has had one, {id}.
explained.tdh.proofs.trust.curve: The curve both proofs are wrapped on
explained.tdh.proofs.trust.curveCovers: Both use {wrapper}, so a break of it would reach both. P52 recommends another curve for program B; open.
explained.tdh.proofs.trust.programsCover: P26's test vectors, the two programs against each other, and the daily comparison with 6529.io.
explained.tdh.proofs.trust.identity: The program keys match their source code
explained.tdh.proofs.trust.identityCover: Each program was rebuilt from source at another path on the same machine, with the same file and key. The code is private (D116), so no one else has rebuilt them.
explained.tdh.proofs.trust.startCovers: Until the history from block {block} is proved, a deployment's first day is taken on trust.
explained.tdh.proofs.trust.hashesCovers: Every anchor rests on them. A reorganisation past an anchor also removes the transaction that used it.
explained.tdh.proofs.trust.rerunCovers: The programs' code and the proof files are private until the owner publishes them ({decision}).
explained.tdh.proofs.trail.heading: Who can check a proof today
explained.tdh.proofs.trail.blocksSub: every header and receipt of the day
explained.tdh.proofs.trail.runsSub: the input, the steps, the words
explained.tdh.proofs.trail.filesSub: kept by 6529 with the validator code
explained.tdh.proofs.trail.verifierSub: one read-only call, given the files
explained.tdh.proofs.trail.wordsSub: printed on this page, from the proof
explained.tdh.proofs.trail.cap: For now the proofs are made and checked by 6529 and read by everyone. Publishing the code and the proof files is the owner's decision.

explained.tdh.proofs.door.sure: Lean proves properties of the rules. A zero-knowledge proof is about one day: what it shows, and how far it has got.
explained.tdh.proofs.door.check: A green day is a strong check. A proof of a day goes further: what it shows, and how far it has got.
